name: Erez Firt
abstract_title: The Undetectable Mind: Why AI Consciousness Will Likely Remain Hidden
abstract: This paper argues that even if AI systems develop genuine consciousness – defined as subjective, qualitative experience in Nagel's (1974) sense of “what it is like” to be that entity – humans will likely fail to detect or accept them as conscious due to fundamental epistemological barriers. This phenomenal dimension, supported by contemporary work on consciousness (Chalmers, 1996; Block, 1995), creates what philosophers call the "hard problem" of consciousness, which resists objective detection
position: Academic Director, Center for Humanities and AI
field: Philosophy of AI / machine ethics / philosophy of mind
notable: Academic Director of Center for Humanities and AI at University of Haifa
notes: Publishes on artificial moral agents, AI understanding, and calibrating machine behavior.
